question.problem: Expressed as a decimal in its simplest form, $(-4.5)^{2}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We need to calculate the product of $(-4.5)$ with itself:

$$
(-4.5)^{2}=(-4.5)\cdot (-4.5)=(4.5)\cdot (4.5)
$$

First, we ignore the decimal points and multiply as if both numbers were whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{2} \\ \boxed{2}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $45\times 45=2\,025.$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in the first factor ($4.5$) and $1$ decimal place in the second factor ($4.5$), so their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

We take our value of $2\,025$ and insert a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places:

$$
20\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{25}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Therefore, $(-4.5)^{2}=20.25\,.$
